objective: Structuring and naming metrics: the _total, _seconds and _bytes conventions, base units, label cardinality limits, and avoiding high-cardinality labels
secondaryObjectives: Instrumentation: what to measure (RED and USE methods), choosing counters and histograms, label choices and bucket boundaries
Client libraries: instrumenting code with the official libraries, exposing /metrics, and the four metric types in code

The company, the services, the metrics and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You review instrumentation changes for the platform team at Copperleaf Energy, a fictional utility. The billing API's first metrics are in a pull request and ship tomorrow. Its owners want request rate, errors and latency (RED) for every endpoint.
handover: The pull request adds: billing_request_time_ms (a gauge set to the last request's time), billing_requests (a counter), and a path label holding the raw URL.
URLs include account numbers, such as /accounts/88123091/invoices.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: in the first invoice run, 8% of requests take 4 s; the gauge happens to sample fast ones and the dashboard stays green.
Check-in 3: the shared Prometheus runs out of memory on the first billing day; every team's alerts stop for two hours.
Check-in 4: request-rate panels show nonsense spikes and the SLO error ratio comes out above 100%.

latPrompt.title: Latency as a gauge in ms
latPrompt.context: Owners want p95 and p99 per endpoint.

choices.label: Replace it with a histogram billing_request_duration_seconds with buckets around the 300 ms target (0.05 to 2.5 s)

effects.log: A seconds histogram with chosen buckets replaces the gauge.

choices.feedback: Durations are observed into a histogram in seconds (the base unit) so quantiles can be computed across instances.

choices.label: Use a summary with p95 and p99 computed in the client
choices.feedback: You get quantiles per instance, but summary quantiles can't be aggregated across instances.

choices.label: Keep the gauge: dashboards can average it
choices.feedback: A gauge of the last request's time samples one request per scrape; the slow tail is invisible.

pathPrompt.title: Raw URLs as a label
pathPrompt.context: 2.4 million accounts would mean millions of series per metric.

choices.label: Label with the framework's route template (/accounts/:id/invoices), never the raw path, and keep status as a bounded class

effects.log: The label is the route template.

choices.feedback: Each unique label set is a series; a route template has a few dozen values, an account number millions.

choices.label: Drop the path label entirely
choices.feedback: Cardinality is safe, but owners can no longer see which endpoint is slow.

choices.label: Ship it with raw paths and add more memory if needed
choices.feedback: Millions of series overwhelm the shared Prometheus that every team's alerts run on.

namesPrompt.title: Counter names and errors
namesPrompt.context: The counter is billing_requests; errors are only visible as status=500.

choices.label: Rename to billing_requests_total, keep a bounded status code class label for errors, and check the names with promtool check metrics

effects.log: Names follow the conventions and pass promtool.

choices.feedback: Counters end in _total, units are base units in the name, and RED is rate, errors and duration from these metrics.

choices.label: Add a separate billing_errors counter and keep billing_requests as it is

effects.log: A second counter for errors is added.

choices.feedback: Errors are countable, but the names break conventions that tools and other teams rely on.

choices.label: Make requests a gauge that the service resets to zero every minute
choices.feedback: rate() on a gauge that resets is meaningless; scrapes miss the values between resets.

parts.criteria: A _seconds histogram for latency; a _total counter for requests; RED from these.
parts.modelAnswer: Latency is a billing_request_duration_seconds histogram; requests a billing_requests_total counter, so rate, errors and duration come from two metrics.

parts.criteria: Route template instead of raw paths; bounded status classes; why cardinality matters.

latHarm.headline: Histograms for latency
latHarm.body: Observe durations into a _seconds histogram so quantiles are possible.

pathHarm.headline: Bounded labels only
pathHarm.body: Never put IDs or raw URLs in labels; use the route template.

namesHarm.headline: Counters for counts

scoring.modelReasoning: Choose the metric type by what it measures: durations into a histogram (aggregatable quantiles) in base units (_seconds), counts into a monotonic counter named _total. Every unique label set is a separate series, so labels must be bounded: a route template, not raw URLs or IDs. RED (rate, errors, duration) for a request-driven service comes from a counter with a bounded status label and a duration histogram.
